Class-conditional distributions of the Swiss validation samples (every glacier pixel
plus the 250 m ring around the outlines) for each measurement layer, as split violins:
glacier above the centre line, non-glacier below, each half with its quartiles and
scaled to the same peak width, so the shapes compare but the heights do not. Only
the pixel values enter, not the 5x5 window statistics the models see. Both polarisations
compare the merged GLACE composites with the per-pass (ascending, descending)
composites and with the Global Seasonal Sentinel-1 Interferometric Coherence and
Backscatter Dataset of Kellndorfer et al. (2022), labelled "Global seasonal", which
has no VH coherence. Every layer is drawn and scored on the same pixels, the common
support: the samples where all layers of the figure are finite, so the pixels the
merged composites fill in but a single pass or the global seasonal product misses are
left out of all of them. The
AUC in the figure and the AUC and JM of the table are the pooled scores of
`scripts/validation/compute-separability.py` over that support (run with the three
dataset configs; `glace_production.validation.separability.common_support` defines it
for both), read from `separability/{dataset}.parquet`;
the violins are drawn from every sample of the support, not a subsample.

```{python}
import colorsys
from string import ascii_lowercase

from matplotlib.colors import to_rgb
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib_inline.backend_inline import set_matplotlib_formats
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d

from glace_production.composites import default_config_dir
from glace_production.config import settings
from glace_production.plotting import add_grid, set_context, set_style
from glace_production.validation.config import DatasetConfig
from glace_production.validation.separability import (
    common_support,
    common_support_name,
    layer_features,
    load_layer_samples,
)
from glace_production.validation.store import ValidationStore

set_style()
set_context("paper")
set_matplotlib_formats("retina")
```

## Configuration

```{python}
FIGURE_NAME = "separability-overview"  # saved as {FIGURE_NAME}.pdf in FIGURE_DIR
FIGURE_DIR = settings.figures_dir / FIGURE_NAME  # one folder per notebook
FIGURE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# The class colours of mapping-examples.qmd; each outline is a stronger shade of its fill
CLASSES = {"Glacier": "#8EB7E0", "Non-glacier": "#DDDDDD"}
OUTLINE_LIGHTNESS = 0.7  # factor on the fill's HLS lightness
OUTLINE_SATURATION = 1.15  # factor on the fill's HLS saturation

# (polarisation, measurement) -> {row label: (dataset, feature)}. A row a panel lacks
# stays empty, so the rows line up across a polarisation.
LAYERS = {
    ("VV", "coherence"): {
        "GLACE": ("lrw-alps", "coh_vv"),
        "Ascending": ("pass-alps", "coh_vv_a"),
        "Descending": ("pass-alps", "coh_vv_d"),
        "Global seasonal": ("globalseasonal-ch", "gs_coh_vv"),
    },
    ("VV", "backscatter"): {
        "GLACE": ("lrw-alps", "rtc_vv"),
        "Ascending": ("pass-alps", "rtc_vv_a"),
        "Descending": ("pass-alps", "rtc_vv_d"),
        "Global seasonal": ("globalseasonal-ch", "gs_bs_vv"),
    },
    ("VH", "coherence"): {
        "GLACE": ("lrw-alps", "coh_vh"),
        "Ascending": ("pass-alps", "coh_vh_a"),
        "Descending": ("pass-alps", "coh_vh_d"),
    },
    ("VH", "backscatter"): {
        "GLACE": ("lrw-alps", "rtc_vh"),
        "Ascending": ("pass-alps", "rtc_vh_a"),
        "Descending": ("pass-alps", "rtc_vh_d"),
        "Global seasonal": ("globalseasonal-ch", "gs_bs_vh"),
    },
}
ROWS = {pol: ["GLACE", "Ascending", "Descending", "Global seasonal"] for pol in ("VV", "VH")}
ROW_LABELS = {"Global seasonal": "Global\nseasonal"}  # broken to keep the left margin narrow
BOLD_ROW = "GLACE"  # the dataset the figure presents, set in bold
MEASUREMENTS = {  # title, x-axis label, x range; the panels from left to right
    # narrow panels tick every 10 dB, so the range ends on 10 to have both ends ticked
    "backscatter": ("Backscatter", "Backscatter (dB)", (-30.0, 10.0)),
    "coherence": ("Coherence", "Coherence", (0.0, 1.0)),
}
LABEL_PANEL = ("VV", "backscatter")  # the class names go beside this panel's first violin
LABEL_OFFSET = 0.25  # of the class names from the centre line, in rows
LABEL_FADE = 0.1  # a name sits where its half has risen to, or fallen to, this share of its peak
LABEL_PAD = 0.005  # between a name and its half, in panel widths

BINS = 400  # density histogram over the x range
SMOOTH_BINS = 2.0  # Gaussian smoothing of the histogram, in bins
HALF_WIDTH = 0.42  # every half is scaled to this peak width, in rows
# Line widths in points: the solid median as heavy as the outline, the dashed quartiles
# lighter, so the median stands out by its weight and its solid line
QUARTILE_WIDTH = 0.5
OUTLINE_WIDTH = 0.7
MEDIAN_WIDTH = 0.7

# Layout in mm; Nature's maximum is 180 mm x 215 mm
MM = 1 / 25.4
FIG_WIDTH = 180
ROW_HEIGHT = 9.0
ROW_PAD = 0.65  # rows of padding above the first and below the last violin
MARGIN_LEFT = 21.5  # polarisation and row labels
POL_LABEL_X = 18.5  # polarisation labels, left of the panels
MARGIN_RIGHT = 2.0
MARGIN_TOP = 6.0  # column titles
MARGIN_BOTTOM = 9.0  # x-axis labels
COLUMN_GAP = 7.0
GROUP_GAP = 0.7  # rows of whitespace between the VV and VH violins

# A narrow panel right of the violins with one AUC dot per row and measurement
DOTS_WIDTH = 44.0
AUC_RANGE = (0.7, 1.0)
AUC_TICKS = (0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0)
DOT_LABEL_OFFSET = 0.2  # of the measurement names from their dots, in rows
DOT_SIZE = 4.0  # points; the line joining a row's dots is as thick
# Mid grey at 16 % reads as 0.92 on white, and lets the gridlines through
DOT_LINE_COLOR = "0.5"
DOT_LINE_ALPHA = 0.16
# The dots, their names and the violin panels' titles share the measurement's colour
MEASUREMENT_COLORS = {"backscatter": "#4a9", "coherence": "#a49"}
```

## Data

```{python}
store = ValidationStore.default()
CONFIG_DIR = default_config_dir() / "validation" / "datasets"
datasets = sorted({d for panel in LAYERS.values() for d, _ in panel.values()})
configs = [DatasetConfig.from_yaml(CONFIG_DIR / f"{d}.yml") for d in datasets]
drawn = {(d, f) for panel in LAYERS.values() for d, f in panel.values()}
assert drawn == {(c.name, f) for c in configs for f in layer_features(c)}, "LAYERS != the layers"

# The common support of compute-separability.py: the rows where every layer is finite
samples = load_layer_samples(store, configs)
samples = samples[common_support(samples, configs)].reset_index(drop=True)
glacier = samples["label"].to_numpy() == 1
print(f"common support: {glacier.sum():,} glacier, {(~glacier).sum():,} non-glacier pixels")

RERUN = "pixi run python scripts/validation/compute-separability.py " + " ".join(
    f"config/validation/datasets/{d}.yml" for d in datasets
)
tables = pd.concat([store.read_parquet(store.separability_path(d)) for d in datasets])
if "support" not in tables.columns:
    raise RuntimeError(f"separability tables predate the common support; rerun: {RERUN}")
pooled = tables[tables.group_by == "all"].set_index(["dataset", "feature"])
# The scores must come from the same support as the violins
scored = pooled.loc[sorted(drawn)]
if not (
    (scored["support"] == common_support_name(configs)).all()
    and (scored["n_glacier"] == glacier.sum()).all()
    and (scored["n_other"] == (~glacier).sum()).all()
):
    raise RuntimeError(f"separability tables are not on this common support; rerun: {RERUN}")


def violin(values: np.ndarray, x_range: tuple[float, float]) -> dict[str, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Smoothed density on the bin centres and quartiles of each class's finite values."""
    edges = np.linspace(*x_range, BINS + 1)
    out = {}
    for name, sel in (("Glacier", glacier), ("Non-glacier", ~glacier)):
        v = values[sel]
        v = v[np.isfinite(v)]
        hist, _ = np.histogram(v, bins=edges)
        out[name] = {
            "x": (edges[:-1] + edges[1:]) / 2,
            "density": gaussian_filter1d(hist / (v.size * np.diff(edges)), SMOOTH_BINS),
            "quartiles": np.quantile(v, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]),
        }
    return out


violins = {
    (pol, kind, row): violin(samples[feature].to_numpy(np.float32), MEASUREMENTS[kind][2])
    for (pol, kind), panel in LAYERS.items()
    for row, (_, feature) in panel.items()
}
```

## Table

Pooled scores of every layer in the figure, with the pixels each is computed over
(the common support, the same for every layer).

```{python}
table = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "polarisation": pol,
            "measurement": kind,
            "product": row,
            "dataset": dataset,
            "feature": feature,
            "auc": pooled.loc[(dataset, feature), "auc"],
            "jm": pooled.loc[(dataset, feature), "jm"],
            "n_glacier": pooled.loc[(dataset, feature), "n_glacier"],
            "n_other": pooled.loc[(dataset, feature), "n_other"],
        }
        for (pol, kind), panel in LAYERS.items()
        for row, (dataset, feature) in panel.items()
    ]
).set_index(["polarisation", "measurement", "product"])
table.style.format({"auc": "{:.3f}", "jm": "{:.3f}", "n_glacier": "{:,}", "n_other": "{:,}"})
```

### LaTeX

The AUC of the table as a booktabs `tabular` (`Styler.to_latex`), one row per layer
and one column per product, the best of each row in bold. Printed for copying and
saved as `{FIGURE_NAME}-table.tex` in `FIGURE_DIR`.

```{python}
PRODUCTS = ROWS["VV"]
auc = table["auc"].unstack("product").reindex(columns=PRODUCTS)
auc = auc.reindex([(pol, kind) for kind in ("coherence", "backscatter") for pol in ("VV", "VH")])
auc.index = [f"{MEASUREMENTS[kind][0]} {pol}" for pol, kind in auc.index]
auc.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([["AUC"], PRODUCTS], names=[None, "Layer"])
latex = (
    auc.style.format("{:.3f}", na_rep="--")
    .highlight_max(axis=1, props="textbf:--rwrap;")
    .to_latex(hrules=True, multicol_align="c", column_format="l" + "c" * len(PRODUCTS))
)
lines = latex.splitlines()
lines.insert(3, rf"\cmidrule(lr){{2-{len(PRODUCTS) + 1}}}")  # below the "AUC" header
latex = "\n".join(lines)
(FIGURE_DIR / f"{FIGURE_NAME}-table.tex").write_text(latex + "\n")
print(latex)
```

## Figure

The AUC as dots in a panel of their own beside the violins; JM is left to the table.

```{python}
def stronger(color: str) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """A darker, more saturated shade of ``color`` for the violin outlines."""
    h, l, s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(*to_rgb(color))
    return colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h, l * OUTLINE_LIGHTNESS, min(1.0, s * OUTLINE_SATURATION))


# Row centres from the top: the polarisations one below the other on one x axis,
# separated by GROUP_GAP rows of whitespace
row_y = {}
y = 0.0
for pol, rows in ROWS.items():
    for row in rows:
        row_y[pol, row] = y
        y -= 1
    y -= GROUP_GAP
y_lim = (min(row_y.values()) - ROW_PAD, ROW_PAD)
panel_height = (y_lim[1] - y_lim[0]) * ROW_HEIGHT
fig_height = MARGIN_TOP + panel_height + MARGIN_BOTTOM


def auc(pol: str, kind: str, row: str) -> float:
    dataset, feature = LAYERS[pol, kind][row]
    return float(pooled.loc[(dataset, feature), "auc"])


def draw_title(ax: plt.Axes, letter: str, title: str, color: str = "black") -> None:
    """Bold ``title`` in ``color`` centred above ``ax``, and the bold panel ``letter`` on
    its baseline above the upper-left corner."""
    ax.set_title(title, fontweight="bold", color=color)
    ax.annotate(
        letter,
        (0, 1),
        xycoords="axes fraction",
        xytext=(0, plt.rcParams["axes.titlepad"]),
        textcoords="offset points",
        ha="left",
        va="baseline",
        fontsize=plt.rcParams["axes.titlesize"],
        fontweight="bold",
    )


def draw_violins(ax: plt.Axes, kind: str, letter: str) -> None:
    """Split violins of one measurement, every row of ``row_y``, on one x axis."""
    title, xlabel, x_range = MEASUREMENTS[kind]
    for (pol, row), y in row_y.items():
        if row not in LAYERS[pol, kind]:
            continue
        halves = violins[pol, kind, row]
        for (name, half), sign in zip(halves.items(), (1, -1), strict=True):
            width = half["density"] * HALF_WIDTH / half["density"].max()
            edge = stronger(CLASSES[name])
            ax.fill_between(half["x"], y, y + sign * width, facecolor=CLASSES[name], linewidth=0)
            ax.plot(half["x"], y + sign * width, color=edge, linewidth=OUTLINE_WIDTH)
            for k, q in enumerate(half["quartiles"]):
                ax.plot(
                    [q, q],
                    [y, y + sign * np.interp(q, half["x"], width)],
                    color=edge,
                    linewidth=MEDIAN_WIDTH if k == 1 else QUARTILE_WIDTH,
                    linestyle="-" if k == 1 else (0, (2, 1.5)),
                    solid_capstyle="butt",
                )
        ax.axhline(y, color="0.3", linewidth=0.4)
        # Class names on the diagonal, as in the separability panel: the glacier name right
        # of its half, where it has fallen off, the non-glacier name left of its half, where
        # it starts to rise
        if (pol, kind) == LABEL_PANEL and row == ROWS[pol][0]:
            pad = LABEL_PAD * (x_range[1] - x_range[0])
            for (name, half), sign in zip(halves.items(), (1, -1), strict=True):
                risen = half["x"][half["density"] > LABEL_FADE * half["density"].max()]
                right = sign == 1
                ax.text(
                    risen[-1] + pad if right else risen[0] - pad,
                    y + sign * LABEL_OFFSET,
                    name,
                    ha="left" if right else "right",
                    va="center",
                    color=stronger(CLASSES[name]),
                )
    ax.set_ylim(*y_lim)
    ax.set_xlim(*x_range)
    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False)
    first = kind == next(iter(MEASUREMENTS))
    ax.set_yticks(
        list(row_y.values()), [ROW_LABELS.get(row, row) for _, row in row_y] if first else []
    )
    for label in ax.get_yticklabels():
        if label.get_text() == BOLD_ROW:
            label.set_fontweight("bold")
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    draw_title(ax, letter, title, MEASUREMENT_COLORS[kind])
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)


def draw_dots(ax: plt.Axes, letter: str) -> None:
    """One AUC dot per row and measurement, joined per row, named on the first row."""
    for (pol, row), y in row_y.items():
        values = {kind: auc(pol, kind, row) for kind in MEASUREMENTS if row in LAYERS[pol, kind]}
        ax.plot(
            list(values.values()),
            [y] * len(values),
            color=DOT_LINE_COLOR,
            alpha=DOT_LINE_ALPHA,
            linewidth=DOT_SIZE,
            solid_capstyle="butt",
            zorder=1,
        )
        for kind, value in values.items():
            ax.plot(
                value,
                y,
                marker="o",
                markersize=DOT_SIZE,
                markeredgewidth=0,
                color=MEASUREMENT_COLORS[kind],
                linestyle="none",
                zorder=2,
            )
            if (pol, row) == next(iter(row_y)):
                # Coherence named above its dot, backscatter below, so the names never meet
                above = kind == "coherence"
                ax.text(
                    value,
                    y + (DOT_LABEL_OFFSET if above else -DOT_LABEL_OFFSET),
                    MEASUREMENTS[kind][0],
                    ha="center",
                    va="bottom" if above else "top",
                    color=MEASUREMENT_COLORS[kind],
                )
    ax.set_ylim(*y_lim)
    ax.set_xlim(*AUC_RANGE)
    ax.set_xticks(AUC_TICKS)
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False)
    add_grid(ax, axis="x", linewidth=0.4)
    draw_title(ax, letter, "Separability")
    ax.set_xlabel("AUC")


def rect(x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Figure-fraction rectangle of a box at (x, y) mm from the top-left corner."""
    return (x / FIG_WIDTH, 1 - (y + height) / fig_height, width / FIG_WIDTH, height / fig_height)


panel_width = (
    FIG_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT - MARGIN_RIGHT - len(MEASUREMENTS) * COLUMN_GAP - DOTS_WIDTH
) / len(MEASUREMENTS)
print(f"figure {FIG_WIDTH} mm x {fig_height:.1f} mm, violin panels {panel_width:.1f} mm wide")
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH * MM, fig_height * MM))
x = MARGIN_LEFT
letters = iter(ascii_lowercase)
for kind in MEASUREMENTS:
    ax = fig.add_axes(rect(x, MARGIN_TOP, panel_width, panel_height))
    draw_violins(ax, kind, next(letters))
    if kind == next(iter(MEASUREMENTS)):
        # Polarisation labels, centred on their rows
        for pol, rows in ROWS.items():
            ax.text(
                -POL_LABEL_X / panel_width,
                np.mean([row_y[pol, r] for r in rows]),
                pol,
                transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),
                rotation=90,
                va="center",
                ha="center",
                fontweight="bold",
                fontsize=plt.rcParams["axes.titlesize"],
            )
    x += panel_width + COLUMN_GAP
draw_dots(fig.add_axes(rect(x, MARGIN_TOP, DOTS_WIDTH, panel_height)), next(letters))
with (FIGURE_DIR / f"{FIGURE_NAME}.pdf").open("wb") as f:
    fig.savefig(f, format="pdf", bbox_inches=None)
```
